subject: Social Media
title: The Attention Tax
description: A 60-second lesson on The Attention Tax.

hook.text: The average person spends 2.5 hours daily on social media. That's 38 full days per year. Gone.

buildup.text: Time is the most obvious cost. But attention fragmentation is worse—your focus shatters across platforms.

discovery.text: Gloria Mark found the average focus span dropped from 2.5 minutes in 2004 to 47 seconds in 2023.

twist.text: Even when not using phones, heavy users show reduced concentration. The habits persist offline.

climax.text: Cal Newport argues this is an attention tax: platforms take focus as payment for 'free' services.

punchline.text: If it's free, your attention is the price.

quiz.question: How much did average focus span drop from 2004 to 2023?
